The audited ledger in `docs/case-studies/issue-183/requirements.md` holds 148 atomic requirements: 95 complete, 31 partial, 19 open, and 3 blocked. Full-language closure, link-executed verification across the whole corpus, comparable alternative foundations, and the native meta-theory workflow remain open.\n\nThis description covers the most recent work, newest first. Every requirement, with its status and evidence, is in the ledger.\n\n## What changed\n\n### One LiNo front end for both runtimes\n\nBoth runtimes now read every `.lino` document through one front end, `js/src/rml-lino-frontend.mjs` and its Rust mirror `rust/src/lino_frontend.rs`, instead of calling `links-notation` 0.20 directly. The front end:\n\n- reads every reference that opens with a quote itself, in one left-to-right pass, and hands the parser a token in its place;\n- hands the parser no piece whose parentheses nest more than two levels deep (`LINO_PIECE_DEPTH`), putting a one-name placeholder where a deeper group stood;\n- refuses a document nested deeper than 64 parenthesis-and-indentation levels (`MAX_LINO_NESTING_DEPTH`) or longer than `MAX_LINO_SOURCE_UNITS` code units, with the parse error `E006`;\n- builds the links of an indented id itself: a line under an indented id keeps its name, and an indented id among those lines reads the way it reads on its own, so `a:` over `b: c` reads as `(a: (b: c))`; a line indented under any other line of an indented id is refused with `E006` instead of being dropped.\n\n`js/tests/lino-frontend.test.mjs` and `rust/tests/lino_frontend_tests.rs` check the same 100 cases in `test-corpus/lino-frontend/cases.json`, read 64 indented ids nested one under another and refuse 65, read twelve sources built to be slow within five seconds each, and keep references made of private-use characters apart from the names the front end makes. `experiments/lino-frontend/differential.mjs`, `deep-documents.mjs`, `quote-reading.mjs`, and `nested-indented-ids.mjs` compare the two front ends over generated documents and find no difference.\n\n### Upstream links-notation reports\n\nReading `links-notation` 0.20 directly on these shapes is why the front end exists. `experiments/lino-frontend/upstream.mjs` shows, in both runtimes, what the parser reads alone and how long it takes. The findings are filed against `link-foundation/links-notation`:\n\n- #312 - the JavaScript and Rust parsers disagree on a lone CR, Unicode spaces, a last line of spaces, and singlets;\n- #313 - lines under an indented id lose their names and their own indented lines;\n- #314 - reading nested groups takes time that grows exponentially with the nesting in both ports, and the Rust `parse_lino_to_links` entry point adds quadratic time by deep-copying the subtree once per level;\n- #315 - a deeply nested document overflows the Rust stack and aborts the process uncatchably, and neither port enforces the nesting-depth limit it documents;\n- #316 - reading a reference that opens with a wide run of quotes takes quadratic time in both ports.\n\nThe three denial-of-service reports, #314 through #316, were filed after the maintainer authorized public reporting (PR comments 5831221597 and 5831357798). The front end already caps source size and nesting depth and reads quoted references itself, so both runtimes stay away from these shapes.\n\n### Selectable type ontology (R129 complete, R114 partial)\n\n`recursive-type-ontology.md` and the mirrored `linkCliInteropProfile` / `link_cli_interop_profile` tests classify the opt-in link-cli type ontology as a candidate default construction, not a premise about what links intrinsically are or a logical `Type : Type` rule (R129, complete). The default is available only through an explicit factory; the mirrored `leaves the default type ontology to the callers that select it` tests find no `Type` link in a bare typed network, no runtime module that selects the default ontology, and an evaluator whose universes stay stratified, answering `Type of Type` only for a source that declares `(Type: Type Type)`. Foundation-declared universe and soundness contracts remain open (R114, partial).\n\n### Foundational orientation audit (R148)\n\nReview `5823272578` is registered as R148 (Partial), with the \"Where consequence orientation can come from\" section added to `foundation-search.md`. The mirrored `orientationAudit` / `orientation_audit` tests ask where the orientation of a consequence could come from without assuming source/target, premise/conclusion, time, rewrite direction, function/argument, cause/effect, truth, or proof, and separate intrinsic asymmetries from observer-chosen ones across automorphism-distinguished structures, same-observation pairs, renaming, faithful representations, and carrier recursion. The result is a finite no-go, `CONSEQUENCE_ORIENTATION_DISTINGUISHED_BUT_NOT_FORCED`: address equality and slot order separate the two candidate orientations but never rank them, because composing any invariant selector with the output swap gives an invariant selector that chooses the opposite orientation. R147 stays Partial; an intrinsic orientation of consequence remains open.\n\n### PR metadata\n\nThe description ends with `Advances #183` and names no issue in a closing directive, because #183 is not complete.
